memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and
say to them: 'A priest must not make himself ceremonially unclean for
any of his people who die'" - Lev 21:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This chapter opens with a rule that feels strange to us. Priests were
not to touch a dead body, even of someone they knew. Why such a
restriction? In Israel, death was the loudest reminder that sin had
entered God's good world. The priest stood at the tabernacle as a
living picture of life, wholeness and God's presence. He could not
carry the marks of death into that holy space.

This was never about the priest being better than others. It was about
the message he carried. His whole life was a signpost pointing to a
God who is separate from decay and death.

Dear friend, notice how carefully God protected the picture. Every
detail mattered because the picture pointed to Someone. Jesus, our
great High Priest, walked right into death. He touched the dead and
raised them. He entered the grave itself and came out alive (Heb
4:14-15; Heb 7:26). What the old priests could not do, He did
completely.

You are now called a royal priesthood (1 Pet 2:9). Not because you
avoid certain rooms, but because Christ has made you clean. Live today
knowing your life carries a message about the God you serve.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What does this law teach me about how seriously God views sin and
   death?
2. In what small ways does my daily life point people to Christ?
3. Am I resting in Christ's holiness rather than trying to earn my own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Jesus went into death so I could be brought
into life. Help me live today in a way that quietly points others to
You. Amen.
